name: Sports & Entertainment Management
notes: Competency areas: the 16 knowledge areas (A-P) and their study-guide objectives in the 2025-26 Sports & Entertainment Management guidelines (National FBLA, updated Nov 2025; source copy: https://www.pafbla.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Sports-and-Entertainment-Management.pdf). The guideline says the event is a team role play with a 100-question, 50-minute objective test. Test weights come from a chart that is an image in the PDF and could not be read, so question counts were spread roughly in proportion to the number of study-guide objectives per area. Group is "case" as requested, though the official format is an objective test plus a role play. Written for practice, not copied from official items.
subs: Promotion, Advertising, and Sponsorship for Sports and Entertainment Industry
Planning, Distribution, Marketing, Pricing, and Selling Sports and Entertainment Events
Leadership and Managing Groups and Teams in the Sports and Entertainment Industry
Management Strategies and Strategic Planning Tools

questions.q: A regional team finds that family buyers cut back sharply when prices rise, while corporate buyers buy suites almost regardless of price. Which pricing approach best fits these findings?
choices: Charge different prices to each segment, such as family discounts alongside premium-priced corporate suite packages
Set one uniform price for all buyers so the pricing structure stays simple
Raise every price to the level corporate buyers are willing to pay
Price every seat at the arena average cost per seat to cover costs
questions.explain: Segmented (differential) pricing matches price to each segment's different sensitivity to price. The trap is assuming one price keeps things simpler at the cost of the segments.

questions.q: A team pays $12 to produce a cap that it sells for $30. What is the markup on cost?
questions.explain: Markup on cost is ($30 - $12) / $12 = 150%. The 60% figure is the margin on the selling price, a different measure.

questions.q: A league groups its fans by how often they attend games, such as heavy, moderate and light users. Which type of market segmentation is this?
questions.explain: Grouping buyers by how they act (attendance or purchase behavior) is behavioral segmentation. Psychographic segmentation uses lifestyle and values.

questions.q: A marketing team reviews fan surveys and attendance trends to guide next season's plans. Which marketing function is the team performing?
questions.explain: Collecting and analyzing market information is one of the traditional marketing functions and supports every planning decision.

questions.q: A stadium's mobile app has stopped growing. Sales have leveled off and several competing apps now offer similar features. In which stage of the product life cycle is the app most likely?
questions.explain: Plateauing sales with intense competition describes maturity. Decline would require falling sales, which the scenario does not state.

questions.q: A team's fans choose ticket packages largely based on advice from friends and online reviews. Which factor best explains this buyer behavior?
questions.explain: Buyer behavior is shaped by reference groups and word of mouth. The scenario describes influence from others, not supply constraints.

questions.q: A club adds its logo to a new sports drink, a product outside its original category. Which branding strategy is this?
questions.explain: Using an established brand name on a new product category is a brand extension. Co-branding combines two brands on one product.

questions.q: An arena sells season tickets for $600 each and sells 2,000 seats, for $1,200,000 in revenue. It cuts the price to $500 and sells 2,600 seats. What happens to total revenue?
questions.explain: New revenue is $500 x 2,600 = $1,300,000, up $100,000. Quantity rises 30% for a 16.7% price cut, so demand is elastic and total revenue rises.

questions.q: A sports drink brand wants to be seen as the first choice for marathon runners rather than casual fans. Which marketing activity is this?
choices: Positioning the brand in the target market's mind
questions.explain: Positioning concerns the image a product holds in customers' minds relative to competitors. Segmentation identifies the group; positioning shapes perception of the brand.

questions.q: Which of the following belongs in a marketing plan?
choices: A situation analysis with marketing objectives and strategies
The arena's construction budget for new seats
The box office staffing schedule for one week
questions.explain: A marketing plan includes a situation analysis, objectives, strategies and tactics. The distractors are operational or financial items outside the plan.

questions.q: A team sets its ticket price slightly below competitors' prices to attract new fans quickly and win share, planning to raise prices later. Which pricing strategy is this?
questions.explain: Penetration pricing sets a low entry price to gain share quickly. Skimming does the opposite, starting high and lowering over time.

questions.q: A city is choosing a site for a 15,000-seat arena. Which factor is a core site-selection criterion?
choices: Access by highway and public transit, with enough parking for peak event days
The number of employees the team plans to hire
The ticket prices set for opening night
questions.explain: Venue selection weighs accessibility, parking and the local market. Staffing, inventory and pricing decisions come after the site is chosen.

questions.q: An event has $60,000 in fixed costs. Tickets sell for $40 and the variable cost per attendee is $10. How many attendees are needed to break even?
questions.explain: Break-even = fixed costs / (price - variable cost per attendee) = $60,000 / $30 = 2,000. Dividing fixed costs by the price alone (1,500) ignores variable costs.

questions.q: A stadium buys event cancellation insurance for a concert. Which risk-management strategy is this?
questions.explain: Insurance shifts the financial consequence of a loss to another party, which is risk transfer. Risk reduction lowers the chance or severity of a loss.

questions.q: Staff expect the heaviest arrival rush at a stadium's gates 30 minutes before kickoff. Which action best applies the principle of safety?
choices: Raise gate prices to spread out arrivals
Open extra entry lanes and staff scanning points for the expected arrival peak
Close the gates until 10 minutes before kickoff
Sell more general admission tickets than the venue has room for
questions.explain: Planning capacity for the peak flow reduces crowd-crush risk. The other options either create or increase the crowding danger.

questions.q: A festival projects $500,000 in ticket revenue and $200,000 in sponsorship revenue. Its expenses are projected at $650,000. What is the projected result?
questions.explain: Total revenue of $700,000 less $650,000 in expenses leaves a $50,000 surplus. Sign errors and omitting one revenue source produce the other options.

questions.q: A city wants to fund a new arena without raising taxes on residents, so it issues bonds repaid from hotel and car rental taxes. What type of financing is this?
choices: Common stock sold by the city
Unsecured personal loans to the team owner
Revenue bonds backed by dedicated tax revenue
An unrestricted federal grant for luxury suites
questions.explain: Revenue bonds are repaid from a specific income stream, here dedicated tourism taxes. The other options are not a recognized way for a city to finance a facility this way.

questions.q: A concession stand sells a hot dog and a drink as a combo for $9, when the items cost $10 separately. Why do operators use this approach?
choices: It removes the need to track inventory
It increases the average spend per customer
It lets the venue skip sales tax
questions.explain: Bundles raise average transaction size even when the bundle price is lower than the sum of the parts. The other options misstate what bundling does.

questions.q: A championship weekend needs security, medical, transport and ticketing teams to coordinate across several agencies. Which management approach best organizes this work?
choices: A single integrated operations plan with one lead responsible for communication
Separate budgets for each agency, with no shared schedule
Delaying coordination until the day of the event
Letting each vendor set its own safety procedures
questions.explain: Major events need one integrated plan, a clear chain of command and shared communication. Uncoordinated or late planning is the trap.

questions.q: A stadium adopts a written opening-day checklist for every staff member. What is the main purpose?
choices: To replace the need for staff training
To ensure consistent, repeatable and safe operating procedures
To reduce the venue's insurance premium directly
To increase the number of seats sold
questions.explain: Standard operating procedures provide consistency and safety. The other options overstate what a checklist does.

questions.q: Before a city selects venues for a new event series, which step should come first?
choices: Set the event's objectives, mission and budget
questions.explain: Planning starts with the development phase: defining objectives, mission and budget before choosing venues or vendors.

questions.q: After a charity 5K, event staff send thank-you messages and results to every participant. Why is this follow-up important?
choices: It is required by the sponsors' contracts
It lowers the permit cost of the next event
It replaces the need for a post-event budget review
It builds loyalty and encourages participants to return for future events
questions.explain: Post-event recognition supports retention and service for future events. The other options invent legal or cost effects the scenario does not imply.

questions.q: A stadium needs 40 ushers for weekend games and has only 25 on its roster. Which HR function is most directly involved?
questions.explain: Forecasting staffing needs and recruiting to fill them is the planning and staffing function of human resources.

questions.q: In a professional sports organization, who negotiates a player's contract terms on the player's behalf?
questions.explain: Agents represent players in contract negotiations. Scouts evaluate talent, general managers make roster decisions, and owners hold the franchise.

questions.q: A venue manager approves refunds and also reconciles the cash drawers that the same person handles. Which HR principle is being violated?
questions.explain: Separating authorization from custody and recordkeeping prevents fraud and error. Orientation and development are unrelated to this control.

questions.q: Under the National Labor Relations Act, which action by an employer during a union organizing drive would be an unfair labor practice?
choices: Negotiating wages with a certified union
Firing employees for joining the union
Hiring seasonal workers for peak weekends
questions.explain: The NLRA protects employees' right to organize, so firing them for union activity is an unfair labor practice. Lawful negotiation and normal hiring are not.

questions.q: A team's HR manager compares its staff turnover and hiring costs with three top franchises to set goals. What technique is this?
questions.explain: Benchmarking measures performance against leading peers. Scenario building explores possible futures rather than current comparisons.

questions.q: A stadium's seasonal event staff quit after each season. Which strategy best improves retention?
choices: Post job openings only on the final day of the season
Offer training pathways and a return-season bonus
Cut hours to the legal minimum
questions.explain: Retention improves when workers see a path forward and a reason to return. The distractors increase turnover or ignore the retention problem.

questions.q: A team gives the first 5,000 fans a free bobblehead at the gate. Which element of the promotion mix is this?
questions.explain: Short-term incentives such as giveaways are sales promotions. Publicity is unpaid media coverage.
questions.sub: Promotion, Advertising, and Sponsorship for Sports and Entertainment Industry

questions.q: An athlete is paid a fee to appear in a television ad for a sports drink. What is this arrangement called?
questions.explain: An endorsement pays a person to promote a product. Sponsorship supports an event or team, and product placement shows a brand within content.
questions.sub: Promotion, Advertising, and Sponsorship for Sports and Entertainment Industry

questions.q: A company pays for the naming rights to a stadium. What is the main benefit to the sponsor?
choices: Free tickets for its executives every season
Brand exposure to the event's audience and association with the team's image
questions.explain: Sponsors buy visibility and image transfer. The other options are not standard benefits of naming rights.
questions.sub: Promotion, Advertising, and Sponsorship for Sports and Entertainment Industry

questions.q: A new arena opening receives a front-page story in the local paper at no cost. What promotional tool produced this coverage?
questions.explain: Publicity is unpaid media coverage. Advertising is paid placement, so this coverage is not advertising even though it helps the brand.
questions.sub: Promotion, Advertising, and Sponsorship for Sports and Entertainment Industry

questions.q: Which sequence correctly lists the steps in developing an effective advertising campaign?
choices: Choose media, create the message, then set objectives
Evaluate results, set the budget, then choose a target audience
Create the message, evaluate results, then set the budget
Set objectives and target audience, set the budget, create the message and choose media, then evaluate results
questions.explain: Campaigns start with objectives and audience, then budget, message and media, and finally evaluation. Starting with media or evaluation is out of order.
questions.sub: Promotion, Advertising, and Sponsorship for Sports and Entertainment Industry

questions.q: A film shows a team's branded sports drink on the table during a scene, for a fee paid to the filmmaker. What is this practice called?
questions.explain: Product placement inserts a brand into entertainment content. An endorsement features a person speaking for the product.
questions.sub: Promotion, Advertising, and Sponsorship for Sports and Entertainment Industry

questions.q: A minor league club holds a Halloween-themed game each October, with sponsor logos on the giveaways. What is the main promotional value of seasonal themed events?
choices: They guarantee higher ticket prices all season
They create repeat attendance and give sponsors a fresh reason to feature their brands
They eliminate the need for regular advertising
They lower the club's fixed costs
questions.explain: Themed events drive repeat visits and sponsor visibility. The other options overstate what a single theme can do.
questions.sub: Promotion, Advertising, and Sponsorship for Sports and Entertainment Industry

questions.q: A sponsor pays $250,000 for a season of signage and wants to compare it with other media. Which measure best evaluates the value of this spend?
choices: Total cost divided by the number of team logos
Cost per thousand impressions compared with alternative media
Ticket revenue earned from the sponsor's guests
The sponsor's share price on opening day
questions.explain: CPM (cost per thousand impressions) allows a like-for-like comparison of media costs. The others are not standard media evaluation measures.
questions.sub: Promotion, Advertising, and Sponsorship for Sports and Entertainment Industry

questions.q: A team pays its players salaries to compete in a league, and fans buy tickets to watch. Which category of sports does this describe?
questions.explain: Players paid salaries in a commercial league are professionals. Collegiate and amateur sports do not pay players this way, and camps are instructional.
questions.sub: Promotion, Advertising, and Sponsorship for Sports and Entertainment Industry

questions.q: A championship final sells out while the number of seats stays fixed and demand grows. What happens to the market price of tickets?
questions.explain: With supply fixed, higher demand pushes prices up. Rising demand does not drive prices to zero.

questions.q: A community sports league is organized as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. Which advantage does this status give?
choices: The right to distribute profits to members
Exemption from federal income tax and eligibility for tax-deductible donations
questions.explain: Section 501(c)(3) status exempts qualifying organizations from federal income tax and lets donors deduct gifts. It does not remove state oversight or allow profit distribution.

questions.q: An arena sells naming rights to a corporation for $2 million a year. How should this be classified for the arena?
questions.explain: Cash the arena receives for granting rights is revenue. It is not an expense, asset or liability of the arena.

questions.q: A venue reports revenue of $800,000, cost of goods sold of $300,000 and operating expenses of $350,000. What is operating income?
questions.explain: Operating income = $800,000 - $300,000 - $350,000 = $150,000. The $450,000 option leaves out cost of goods sold.

questions.q: A team reports total assets of $10 million and total liabilities of $6 million. What is owner's equity?
questions.explain: Assets = liabilities + owner's equity, so equity = $10M - $6M = $4M.

questions.q: Which budgeting technique requires every expense to be justified from zero each budget cycle, rather than adjusted from last year's amounts?
questions.explain: Zero-based budgeting rebuilds each budget from scratch. Incremental budgeting starts from the prior year and adjusts it.

questions.q: A city's report claims a tournament generated $40 million in economic impact. It counts all spending, including money local residents would have spent in town anyway. What is the main flaw?
choices: It ignores the multiplier effect of spending
It uses too few years of data
It does not net out substitution effects, where the spending would have happened locally anyway
It counts only ticket revenue and not sponsorships
questions.explain: Credible impact studies subtract spending that merely shifts from other local activities. The multiplier is a legitimate part of the analysis, so ignoring it is not the flaw.

questions.q: A facility's annual lease payment is the same whether or not any events are held. How should this cost be classified?
questions.explain: A cost that does not change with activity in the short run is fixed. Variable costs rise with event volume.

questions.q: A rural minor league team earns most of its revenue in summer. Why should its owner forecast cash flow monthly rather than only annually?
choices: Off-season months can produce cash shortfalls even when the full year is profitable
Monthly forecasts are required by the U.S. tax code
Summer revenue is recorded as a liability until the season ends
Monthly forecasts replace the need for a balance sheet
questions.explain: Profit is measured over the year, but cash must cover bills in the months with little income. The other options misstate accounting or tax rules.

questions.q: Which term describes the process in which an initial spending increase generates further rounds of spending in the local economy?
questions.explain: The multiplier effect explains how each round of spending creates income that is spent again. Substitution is the opposite concern in impact studies.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a ticket broker and a ticket scalper?
choices: A broker sells only at face value, while a scalper sells above face value
A scalper is licensed by the venue, while a broker is not
A broker works only with season-ticket holders, while a scalper works with the public
A broker is a licensed reseller that follows venue and local rules, while a scalper resells tickets illegally or in violation of local law
questions.explain: Licensed brokers operate legally within the rules. Scalpers operate outside them. Reversing the licensing or pricing roles is the trap.
questions.sub: Planning, Distribution, Marketing, Pricing, and Selling Sports and Entertainment Events

questions.q: A venue raises ticket prices closer to game day as seats sell out and demand grows. Which pricing approach is this?
questions.explain: Dynamic pricing adjusts price to real-time demand. Cost-plus pricing sets price from cost, and a price ceiling is a government limit.
questions.sub: Planning, Distribution, Marketing, Pricing, and Selling Sports and Entertainment Events

questions.q: A venue sets its premium seats at a very high launch price for early buyers, then lowers the price over time as more buyers enter. Which strategy is this?
questions.explain: Skimming captures buyers willing to pay the most first, then lowers prices to reach price-sensitive buyers. Penetration does the reverse.
questions.sub: Planning, Distribution, Marketing, Pricing, and Selling Sports and Entertainment Events

questions.q: Before setting a price for a new event package, which step should a planner take first?
choices: Print the price on all advertising
Define pricing objectives and estimate costs and likely demand
Match the rival venue's price exactly
Set the price after the event is held
questions.explain: Pricing starts with objectives, cost and demand estimates. Copying a competitor or pricing after the fact skips the analysis.
questions.sub: Planning, Distribution, Marketing, Pricing, and Selling Sports and Entertainment Events

questions.q: In the sales process, which step comes directly before the presentation?
choices: The approach, the first contact with the prospect
questions.explain: The sequence runs prospecting, preapproach, approach, presentation, then objections and close. The approach precedes the presentation.
questions.sub: Planning, Distribution, Marketing, Pricing, and Selling Sports and Entertainment Events

questions.q: A corporate client buys 20 suites to thank clients and motivate its employees. What is this use of sports and entertainment called?
questions.explain: Corporate hospitality uses events to entertain clients and reward staff. The other options are different business practices.
questions.sub: Planning, Distribution, Marketing, Pricing, and Selling Sports and Entertainment Events

questions.q: A city imposes a legal maximum on the price of parking near a stadium on game days. What type of government influence on pricing is this?
choices: A subsidy paid to the venue
A sales tax paid by the venue
questions.explain: A legal maximum price is a price ceiling. A price floor sets a minimum, and a subsidy or tax does not set the price directly.
questions.sub: Planning, Distribution, Marketing, Pricing, and Selling Sports and Entertainment Events

questions.q: During a recession, which entertainment spending is typically most at risk of decline?
choices: Premium luxury suite and VIP package purchases
questions.explain: Discretionary, high-priced spending falls first in a downturn, while low-cost and community activities hold up better.
questions.sub: Planning, Distribution, Marketing, Pricing, and Selling Sports and Entertainment Events

questions.q: Which U.S. federal law requires public accommodations, including stadiums and arenas, to provide accessible seating for people with disabilities?
choices: Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972
questions.explain: Title III of the ADA covers places of public accommodation, including sports and entertainment venues.

questions.q: Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 primarily prohibits what?
choices: Sex-based discrimination in federally funded education programs, including athletics
questions.explain: Title IX bans sex discrimination in federally funded education programs, including school and college athletics.

questions.q: A promoter uses a copyrighted song in a video ad without permission. Which exclusive right of the copyright owner is most directly infringed?
choices: The right to set the song's ticket price
The right to reproduce and publicly perform the work
The right to collect the venue's concession revenue
The right to name the promoter's company
questions.explain: Copyright gives the owner exclusive rights to reproduce, distribute and publicly perform the work. The distractors are not copyright rights.

questions.q: Under U.S. common law, which three elements are generally required for a valid contract?
choices: Consideration, a written copy and a fee
questions.explain: A valid contract generally needs an offer, acceptance and consideration (something of value exchanged). Notarization and seals are not general requirements.

questions.q: A league rule forbids its teams from negotiating with outside broadcasters, which reduces competition and raises prices. Which body of law is primarily at issue?
choices: Antitrust law, including the Sherman Act
Labor law under the NLRA only
questions.explain: Restraints that reduce competition among firms raise antitrust concerns under the Sherman Act. Labor law and copyright do not address this market restraint.

questions.q: A union's members collectively refuse to work to pressure an employer. What is this action called?
questions.explain: A strike is a collective work stoppage by employees. A lockout is initiated by the employer, and arbitration and grievances are dispute procedures.

questions.q: Which statement best describes publicity?
choices: Paid placement of a message in media
Unpaid media coverage of an organization or event
A sales incentive offered to customers
A contract to use a person's image
questions.explain: Publicity is earned, unpaid media coverage. Paid placement is advertising.

questions.q: A team hires a popular athlete to front its campaign. What is the main benefit the brand gains from this celebrity endorsement?
choices: Guaranteed ticket sales for each game
Lower production costs for the broadcast
Transfer of the celebrity's credibility and appeal to the brand
questions.explain: Endorsements work by transferring a celebrity's credibility and appeal to the brand. The other options are not benefits of endorsement.

questions.q: A star player is arrested for a DUI on the night before a playoff game. What is the best first communication step for the team?
choices: Say nothing until the court case is resolved
Blame the media for the coverage
Post highlight videos to change the focus
Issue a timely, honest statement that acknowledges the facts and describes next steps
questions.explain: Crisis communication works best when the organization is prompt, honest and clear about next steps. Silence or deflection erodes trust.

questions.q: Which media channel gives a team the most direct control over its message?
choices: Its own website and social media accounts
Fan blogs run by outside writers
questions.explain: Owned channels let the organization decide content and timing. Earned media is controlled by journalists and writers.

questions.q: A team employee bets on the team's games. Which ethical concern is most directly raised?
choices: Conflict of interest and threat to the integrity of competition
Failure to pay the employee overtime
questions.explain: An insider betting on outcomes creates a conflict of interest and threatens the integrity of the competition. The other concerns are real but not the central ethical issue.

questions.q: An arena donates part of its concession profits to a youth sports program. Which concept does this best illustrate?
questions.explain: Voluntary action that benefits society beyond legal requirements is corporate social responsibility.

questions.q: A venue's advertising shows premium seats with unobstructed views, but many of those seats have pillars that block the view. What is the likely consequence of this behavior?
choices: A permanent increase in ticket sales
Loss of customer trust and possible legal liability for misleading advertising
questions.explain: Misleading advertising damages trust and can create legal exposure. The other options describe benefits that unethical behavior does not produce.

questions.q: A team's licensee pays the team 8% of the wholesale price of each licensed jersey it sells. What is this payment called?
questions.explain: A royalty is a payment, usually a percentage of sales, for the right to use intellectual property.

questions.q: A video game publisher pays a team a fee to use its logos and team names in a game. What arrangement is this?
choices: A sponsorship of the publisher's events
An endorsement contract for the team's coach
A joint venture to build a stadium
questions.explain: Granting permission to use logos and names for a fee is a licensing agreement. The other arrangements involve different rights or purposes.

questions.q: A team earns $1,200,000 in royalties at an 8% royalty rate. What were the licensed sales?
questions.explain: Licensed sales = royalties / rate = $1,200,000 / 0.08 = $15,000,000.

questions.q: Which body governs member four-year colleges and universities in Divisions I, II and III of U.S. collegiate athletics?
questions.explain: The NCAA sets rules for its member colleges and universities across its three divisions. The others govern professional leagues or tours.

questions.q: A two-year community college wants its teams to compete under a national governing body for junior colleges. Which organization should it join?
questions.explain: The NJCAA governs athletics for U.S. two-year colleges. The NAIA serves small four-year institutions.

questions.q: Which role enforces a professional league's rules and resolves disputes among its member teams?
choices: The head of a team's ticketing department
questions.explain: The commissioner is the league's chief executive, responsible for enforcing rules and settling disputes among teams.

questions.q: A league limits its official beverage sponsorship to one company per category. What is the main benefit of this exclusivity?
choices: It removes the need for any sponsorship revenue
It lets the league avoid all antitrust review
It lets each team set sponsorship prices alone
It protects the sponsor's investment by keeping competitors from diluting the brand
questions.explain: Category exclusivity protects what the sponsor pays for. The other options misstate what the rule does.

questions.q: Which item belongs in a career portfolio for a sports management applicant?
choices: A list of personal social media passwords
A résumé with work samples and a cover letter
A copy of a current employer's confidential budget
questions.explain: A career portfolio presents qualifications: résumé, cover letter and work samples. The other items are private or confidential.

questions.q: A recent graduate wants to enter the sports and entertainment industry. Which entry-level position is most typical?
choices: Chief executive of a professional league
General manager of a professional franchise
questions.explain: Entry-level roles in event and ticket operations build experience. The other positions require years of experience.

questions.q: A candidate lacks industry experience for a sports marketing job. Which strategy best overcomes this barrier?
choices: Apply only to positions that require no experience
Omit the education section of the résumé
Complete a volunteer role or internship that builds relevant event experience
Wait until the posting closes before applying
questions.explain: Relevant volunteer work and internships address the experience gap directly. The other options avoid the problem.

questions.q: A stadium uses one system that links ticketing, concession sales and attendance. What is the main purpose of this management information system?
choices: To set the official league schedule
To sell advertising directly to fans
To give managers timely information to support decisions
questions.explain: An MIS collects and organizes data so managers can make timely, informed decisions.

questions.q: A team wants every fan in its database to have an equal chance of being surveyed. Which sampling method does this?
questions.explain: Simple random sampling gives every member of the population an equal chance of selection. The other methods do not.

questions.q: Offering a 10% discount this Tuesday to boost weekday attendance is an example of what?
choices: A marketing tactic supporting a broader strategy
questions.explain: Tactics are short-term actions that support a strategy. A one-day discount is not a permanent policy.

questions.q: A club wants to test whether a new pregame promotion raises attendance. Which research design is best?
choices: A controlled experiment comparing games with and without the promotion
A focus group after the season ends
A review of last season's ticket sales
A single survey of season-ticket holders
questions.explain: A controlled comparison isolates the promotion's effect. The other designs cannot show cause and effect.

questions.q: Which is an electronic method of collecting fan data?
choices: An online survey or app-based poll
A paper questionnaire mailed to fans
A phone call from the ticket office
questions.explain: Online surveys and app polls collect data electronically. The other methods are paper-based or personal.

questions.q: A manager makes decisions alone and gives staff little input. Which leadership style is this?
questions.explain: The autocratic style centralizes decisions with the leader. The democratic style invites staff input.
questions.sub: Leadership and Managing Groups and Teams in the Sports and Entertainment Industry

questions.q: A new event coordinator needs close direction, while a veteran needs only occasional check-ins. Which leadership approach fits this?
questions.explain: Situational leadership adjusts the leader's style to each follower's readiness. Using one style for both ignores the difference.
questions.sub: Leadership and Managing Groups and Teams in the Sports and Entertainment Industry

questions.q: In Herzberg's motivation theory, which factor is a motivator rather than a hygiene factor?
questions.explain: Motivators such as recognition and achievement increase satisfaction. Hygiene factors such as pay, safety and policies prevent dissatisfaction.
questions.sub: Leadership and Managing Groups and Teams in the Sports and Entertainment Industry

questions.q: A team is formed from marketing, ticketing and operations staff to plan a championship parade. What type of team is this?
questions.explain: Members drawn from several functions form a cross-functional team. A virtual team is defined by remote collaboration, which the scenario does not describe.
questions.sub: Leadership and Managing Groups and Teams in the Sports and Entertainment Industry

questions.q: A group has unclear goals, and its members avoid disagreement to keep the peace. Which is the most likely reason the team will fail?
choices: Unclear goals and roles, combined with suppressed conflict
questions.explain: Teams fail when goals and roles are unclear and healthy conflict is avoided. The distractors are not typical causes of failure.
questions.sub: Leadership and Managing Groups and Teams in the Sports and Entertainment Industry

questions.q: What is a key disadvantage of group decision making?
choices: Groups are unable to reach any decision
Groupthink can suppress dissent and lead to poor choices
questions.explain: Groupthink, the suppression of dissent in the pursuit of harmony, is a major risk of group decisions. The other options are not typical disadvantages.
questions.sub: Leadership and Managing Groups and Teams in the Sports and Entertainment Industry

questions.q: A league decides to expand into two new countries. Which level of strategy does this decision represent?
questions.explain: Corporate strategy defines the overall scope of the enterprise, including which markets it enters. Business-level strategy concerns competing within one unit.
questions.sub: Management Strategies and Strategic Planning Tools

questions.q: In a SWOT analysis of an arena, a new competitor arena opening nearby is classified as what?
questions.explain: An external factor that could hurt the arena is a threat. Strengths and weaknesses are internal.
questions.sub: Management Strategies and Strategic Planning Tools

questions.q: Which sequence correctly describes the strategic management process?
choices: Implement first, then formulate, then evaluate
Formulate the strategy, implement it, then evaluate and control
questions.explain: The strategic management process runs formulation, implementation, then evaluation and control. Implementing before formulating reverses the logic.
questions.sub: Management Strategies and Strategic Planning Tools

questions.q: A premium arena adds budget family concession packages that conflict with its luxury image. What does this illustrate?
choices: A lack of strategic fit between the new offering and the venue's positioning
questions.explain: Strategic fit means new offerings support the organization's positioning. A conflicting offering weakens the brand even if it adds sales.
questions.sub: Management Strategies and Strategic Planning Tools

questions.q: Which strategic planning tool plots business units by market growth rate and relative market share?
questions.explain: The BCG matrix classifies units as stars, cash cows, question marks or dogs using growth and share. The other tools serve different purposes.
questions.sub: Management Strategies and Strategic Planning Tools

questions.q: Which set lists the four basic functions of management?
questions.explain: The four functions of management are planning, organizing, leading (directing) and controlling.

questions.q: A stadium sets a target of 95% on-time gate openings, tracks results, and adjusts staffing when the target is missed. Which control step is the staffing adjustment?
questions.explain: Control runs establish standards, monitor results and compare them, then correct deviations. Adjusting staffing is the correction step.

questions.q: In the decision-making process, which step comes first?
questions.explain: Good decisions start by defining the problem. Choosing, implementing and evaluating come later in the process.

questions.q: A manager delegates the event budget to an assistant but keeps final approval authority. What does the manager retain after delegating?
choices: No responsibility, since the task was delegated
Only the right to change the assistant's title
Full personal liability for every expense line
questions.explain: Authority can be delegated, but the manager stays accountable for results. Delegation does not remove responsibility.

questions.q: Which description best defines economic efficiency for an entertainment event?
choices: Maximizing the number of free tickets given away
Spending the full budget each year
Charging the highest price the market will bear
Producing the event's output at the lowest possible cost
questions.explain: Economic efficiency means getting the most output from given resources, which is achieved at the lowest cost for that output.

questions.q: A venue group uses a divisional structure with separate arena, hotel and concessions units. What is the main advantage?
choices: Each unit avoids all reporting requirements
Each unit can focus on its market and be held accountable for its results
The group no longer needs a chief executive
All units share one budget line
questions.explain: Divisional structures let each unit focus on its market and be measured on its own results. The other options describe drawbacks or misreadings.
